newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling front defers meeting on oil prices.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling front defers meeting on oil prices.

text.p: India's ruling United Front has decided to postpone its meeting on oil prices scheduled for Tuesday, front officials said on Monday.
"The Steering Committee meeting has been deferred," a UF official told Reuters.
He said no new date for the meeting has been fixed.
The official gave no reason for the postponement of the crucial meeting.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the postponement followed reservations by members of the the 15 party coalition over former Janata Dal leader Laloo Prasad Yadav's continued presence in the United Front after he split his party on Saturday.
Yadav, who is mired in a corruption scandal, led a breakaway group from the Janata Dal but has vowed to continue support for Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral.
The meeting called for Tuesday has been deferred twice already.

The steering committee's last two sessions failed to determine what to do about the oil pool account deficit -- the money owed to oil companies for selling petroleum products below market prices to support India's subsidy regime.
